row.scenario: A short Chinese term, a mixed code identifier, negation, punctuation
row.required_outcome: Valid query handling and measured recall; no whole-message AND failure

design: §5 step 3: normalize, keep exact identifiers and paths beside normalized terms, union of terms, literal AST never a caller MATCH expression

§5 step 4 (03 rev 7.8, 09 §6.5): the unicode61 table takes every term — its text and phrases split at script boundaries — as a prefix query when its last token has three or more characters, unless the term carries an unsegmented character or that token is a stop word; the trigram tables hold titles, aliases and tags, and the bodies of unsegmented-script chunks, which only a term carrying such a character searches; phrases and exact identifiers are phrases on the unicode61 table and literals on the header trigram table; 1–2 character queries by a bounded scoped substring pass with `partial`
notes_for_implementer: Four notes and a decoy. The queries mix a short Chinese term, a `SCREAMING_SNAKE` environment variable, a `crate::module` path, a negated sentence and shell punctuation; each must be handled as a valid literal query (no FTS5 syntax error, no empty result because one word of the message is missing) and find its note by the union rule. Negation is not interpreted: the query `not tabs` returns the note that says `Do not use tabs`, and the loader checks the excerpt keeps the `not`. `match_includes` names the reason the design determines (an alias hit is `alias`, an exact identifier is `phrase` or `term`); for the 1- and 2-character CJK substring pass the design names no MatchReason, so those steps check the id only. The decoy (apples) must never appear.
